rationale.complete: Round 1 plus round 1b: all 35 non-holdout periods and NE14 re-run on the corrected activity and outage tables, DQ8-calibrated null added (trim before surrogates; trimmed block-shift edge for lambda_1), three period-native tests (NE43 bookend stop, #4d restart, NE14/#36 with the corrected null). Holdout not run; API outages untested.
rationale.faithfulness: The literal hypothesis still fails (P1, P3, P4 as written, P8; NE43 refutes the operator-message version of the day-edge mechanism; the #4d stop leaves no trace). The partial result is sharper on corrected data: regime-III co-activation is 70-80% day-edge synchrony (f_scaffold 0.72, f_trim 0.83; only #44, #51 and marginally #37 survive the calibrated null), P5, P6 and NE14 pass. C = 1, D = 1, E = 1.
rationale.usefulness: A log-only preprocessing rule with a calibrated null behind it: trim each day to the all-present window before drawing surrogates (DQ8: 28-34% false positives without it, 2-4% with it). NE43 shows the edges come from the runner, so the rule needs runner start/stop times or agent spans, not operator messages. Defensive payoff; blind to API outages.

one_line: Joint silences are rare and operator-scheduled, not platform stalls; in the always-on regime 70-80% of co-activation is the runner's daily start and stop.
